plan: [No prior rounds to learn from. With 5 bidders and third-price payment, the third-order statistic of five uniform draws has mean ~24.5, so bidding my true value is a safe, near-optimal strategy: it wins when the third-highest is below my value and avoids overbidding risk that could produce negative payoff. I will bid my private value to maximize expected surplus while keeping downside limited.]

[Third-price auction with 5 bidders incentivizes systematic overbidding. Assume symmetric linear bids b(v)=αv. With 4 opponents, probability win if bidding as-if t is t^4 and expected third-price (second-highest of 4 others) conditional on max<t is (3/5)t, so payoff ∝ t^4(v - α*(3/5)t). First-order condition gives best-response t=4v/(3α). Symmetry implies α=4/3, so equilibrium b(v)=(4/3)v. For v=$28, bid = (4/3)*28 = $37.333…, round to nearest $0.1 = $37.3.]

[I will bid my true private value of $22. In a third-price auction, bidding your value avoids paying more than the item is worth while still letting you win when your value is sufficiently high. There is no prior history to exploit this round, so truthful bidding is a safe, long-run profit-maximizing baseline under uncertainty about other bidders' strategies. Bid is in $0.1 increments: 22.0.]

[Third-price auction: the winner pays the third-highest bid. With value v=$2 and four independent opponents (uniform 0–49), the probability the third-highest bid is below $2 is negligible, so winning would almost certainly yield negative profit. To maximize long-run profit, avoid winning: submit the minimal bid (0) to guarantee zero payoff instead of likely losses.]

[I maximize expected profit. With five bidders and third-price payment, if others bid their values (uniform 0–49) then win prob = (b/49)^4 and conditional payment ≈ 0.6b (second-highest of four opponents). Expected profit = (b/49)^4*(27 - 0.6b). Differentiating gives optimum b = 36. I therefore bid $36 (0.1 increments allowed). This bids above my value because the third-price rule makes the expected price I pay considerably lower than my bid, raising win chances profitably.]
